key_insight: TCMClinicalReason-Bench shows that language models can produce structurally complete TCM cases while still lacking patient-grounded reasoning from pathogenesis to prescription.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark highlights where clinician review is most needed—especially for prescription generation and case-specific treatment modifications in real-world TCM workflows.
method: Built a 2,000-case multicenter EHR benchmark for TCM clinical reasoning.
Evaluated 7 LLMs in zero-shot settings with an evidence-constrained rubric covering 7 components and 3 cross-block relations.
Compared automated judging with blinded review from 5 senior TCM clinicians on a 600-case subset.
evidence_signal: Structural completeness was near perfect (99.3%-100.0%), but normalized content scores were only 40.7%-54.1%, with moderate correlation between cross-block logic and content (r=0.515-0.656).
watch_item: The automated judge can miss some inconsistencies, especially omissions, so deployment should include human oversight rather than relying on endpoint scores alone.
paper_title: TCMClinicalReason-Bench: Can Language Models Reason from Pathogenesis to Prescription over Real-World Clinical Cases?
